newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Lehman raises Teva EPS estimate.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Lehman raises Teva EPS estimate.

text.p: Lehman Brothers has raised its 1996 full-year earnings forecast for Israel's Teva Pharmaceutical Industries to $1.41 per American depositary receipt (ADR) from $1.38.

Analyst Richard Silver said he raised his estimate after the company reported third-quarter earnings per share (EPS) of $0.39 on Monday, exceeding his projected $0.35. He attributed the earnings surprise to improved gross margins, which more than offset higher costs.

Silver held to his fourth-quarter estimate of $0.47 a share but said the quarter should be strong because Teva has introduced a new generic version of the drug Carafate and because of continued costs savings from its merger with Biocraft.
"The solid third-quarter earnings report, in the face of generic industry pricing pressures, should help allay investor concerns about Teva's base business," Silver said.

"We see the opportunity for significant capital appreciation in 1997, as Teva's growth rate dramatically accelerates," he added. Lehman's 12-18 month price target is "at least" $70, compared to the current $46 Nasdaq price.
